name: Camera Motion
author: Jojocodex
licence: The author publishes this file under Apache-2.0. It was trained on MiniMax H3, whose Community License Agreement (territory limits, Acceptable Use Policy) still governs the base model you run it on.
what: Camera moves the base model tends to miss: push-in, pull-back, orbit, tracking, aerial, crane, pan, macro.
notes: Write the prompt as: subject, place, the camera move, light and style. Name the move in plain words, for example 'slow push-in with subtle lateral tracking' or 'slow pull-back combined with a gentle orbit'. 0.8 is gentle, 1.0 is definite, above 1.2 the picture can turn unstable. The author's page has a library of 55 prompts. The Camera move choices are the author's own phrases, with the author's note on how steady each is; the phrase is added to the prompt after the trigger.

name: Equirectangular 360°
author: shamanic

styles.360° layout: Equirectangular 360-degree panoramic video: the frame is a full spherical projection, a complete environment wrapping around the viewer on all sides, with the horizon at the vertical middle of the frame.

licence: The weights are a Model Derivative of MiniMax H3 under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement, with its territory limits, commercial terms and Acceptable Use Policy. Read the licence on the LoRA's page before downloading.
what: A full-sphere 360° panorama video with sound, for VR players.
notes: Made for a 21:9 frame: pick Custom size, 1120x480. The whole frame is the sphere: resize the clip to 2:1 and add 360 metadata for a VR player. Describe the place, the motion and the sound; a still camera works best. Seams at the wrap and stretching at the poles can still happen.

name: 360° Orbit
author: pablodawson
licence: The weights are a Model Derivative of MiniMax H3 under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement, with its territory limits, commercial terms and Acceptable Use Policy. Read the licence on the LoRA's page before downloading.
what: One photo becomes a frozen-moment 360° orbit that ends on the frame it started from.
notes: Give the same picture as the first and the last frame (step 2, 'Same as the first frame') and use the author's prompt as it is. Author's settings: 768x768, 73 frames, 28 passes, strength 1.0, no sound. It also orbited here at the Studio's usual passes.
prompt: One frozen instant. Only the camera moves. In a continuous 360 orbit. Preserve every person and object in exactly the same world position, orientation, shape and pose throughout the shot. Airborne objects remain suspended at the captured height and angle: no wobbling, shaking, spinning, drifting, falling or continued action. Keep faces, hands, clothing, liquids and the background motionless while retaining their natural appearance. Camera parallax is the only source of apparent movement. No cuts, zoom, morphing or added objects.

notes: Give the start picture as the first frame and the target as the last frame (step 2), and use the author's prompt. Strength 1.0 to 1.2.

name: Multiple Angles (image)
author: akhaliq
licence: The author publishes this file under Apache-2.0. It runs on Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, which is under the Qwen Research License Agreement: non-commercial use only.
what: Shows the subject of a picture from another camera angle: 12 directions at 4 heights, each also as a close-up. It works in Create, Edit a picture, where it adds a camera ring.
notes: Prompt shape: '<mva> front-right quarter view, eye-level shot'; the camera ring writes it. v2, step 1500, is the file the author recommends. Trained on single objects and characters: side and back views often come back on a plain background. Lower the strength towards 0.8 if a result copies your picture. A picture of a whole scene is often reduced to one thing in it on a plain background (measured on both machines). Measured here on Turbo's 8 steps: the quarter views turn the way asked, but a straight left side view and a straight right side view can come out facing the same way. The author's own setting is 40 steps on the base model (the installers' --image-edit adds it; not measured here).
